title: Standing Order on Admission of Pieces and Signing of Reports, Belrose Appraisal and Gemological Services
content:
# Standing Order: Admission of Pieces and Signing of Reports

1. A piece is taken in only at a service whose ceiling on declared value covers what it is worth, and the declared value is what the chain answers for while the piece is in its care. The ceiling on declared value and the amount the chain answers for are fixed per service of Belrose Appraisal and Gemological Services.
2. Examination of a piece is begun only on an engagement that stands at item received or in examination, that is, while the piece is in the appraiser's care as the engagement record under its appraisal reference shows, and the declared value the piece is held at is the value on that record. The engagement record decides this; the customer's account of where the piece is does not.
3. An appraisal states a value for one of the purposes the service offers, and a value stated for one purpose is never read as a value for another.
4. The report is signed only by an appraiser holding the standing the service requires, and at the services that require it a second appraiser reviews the report before it is signed.
5. Where the piece is worth more than the highest ceiling any service carries, the desk does not take it in and the customer is directed to the chain's portfolio appraisal by appointment.
6. A verbal counter estimate states no value in writing and is never accepted by the insurance desk or the upgrade desk in place of a signed report.
7. Whether a piece is taken in by appointment only, whether the appraiser attends the customer's home, and the travel fee for the appraiser attending away from a store are fixed per service.

## Stage at which examination begins

| Engagement stands at | Examination begun |
|---|---|
| Requested | No, the piece is not yet in care |
| Item received | Yes |
| In examination | Yes |
| Report drafted, issued, delivered, expired or cancelled | No |

## Illustrations on a hypothetical ceiling

On a service whose ceiling on declared value is a hypothetical 50000, a piece declared at 50000 is within the ceiling and is taken in; a piece declared at 50001 is above it and is not taken in at that service. A piece worth more than the highest ceiling any service carries is not taken in at any service, and the customer is directed to the chain's portfolio appraisal by appointment.

## Questions answered

**A report states a value for insurance replacement. May that figure be read as the piece's fair market value?** No. A value stated for one purpose is never read as a value for another.

**A customer holding a verbal counter estimate asks whether the insurance desk will take it as their appraisal.** It will not. A verbal counter estimate states no value in writing and is never accepted by the insurance desk or the upgrade desk in place of a signed report.

**May an appraiser of lower standing sign where a second appraiser has reviewed the report?** No. The signing appraiser holds the standing the service requires; the second review, where the service requires it, is in addition to that and not in place of it.
